population_note_text: Books population (optional, cancelled and post-dated vouchers excluded). A capital-ledger line is excluded from the daily-balance walk, and counted as interest/remuneration credited instead, iff that SAME voucher also carries a line on the partner's own interest or remuneration ledger -- identified from the voucher's other lines, never from a date, number or narration.

figures.definition_text: s.40(b) allowable interest for partner (tag 6d3236ec): simple interest at 1200 bp on the capital balance walked day by day (opening TB balance, then every population voucher line on the capital ledger(s) other than an interest/remuneration credit, changing the balance ON its date), actual days / 365, a debit (negative) capital day contributing zero. Not usable for s.40(b): s.40(b) is not computed for this partner (see the finding that says so).
Same daily-balance walk for partner (tag 6d3236ec), but actual days / 360. Not usable for s.40(b): s.40(b) is not computed for this partner (see the finding that says so).

s.40(b) interest for partner (tag 6d3236ec) as if capital were never reduced by a withdrawal or transfer (every debit line on the capital ledger(s) skipped; a credit/increase line, e.g. capital introduced, still applied). Not usable for s.40(b): s.40(b) is not computed for this partner (see the finding that says so).

s.40(b) interest for partner (tag 6d3236ec) as if the capital balance stayed at its opening value for the whole year (no intra-year voucher line applied at all). Not usable for s.40(b): s.40(b) is not computed for this partner (see the finding that says so).

Whether s.40(b)/s.194T apply to this engagement: read from rules.entity(...).s40b_interest_rate_bp and rules.entity(...).s194t for this engagement's entity_type -- never from the entity_type string itself. 'no' when both are absent/zero/false.
Opening (1-4) balance of partner (tag 6d3236ec)'s capital ledger(s), Dr+/Cr-.

Interest actually credited to partner (tag 6d3236ec)'s capital ledger(s), in a voucher also carrying a line on their interest_ledger. Not usable for s.40(b): s.40(b) is not computed for this partner (see the finding that says so).
Rate used for s.40(b) allowable interest: min(deed interest_rate_bp 1200, rules s40b_interest_rate_bp 1200).
Remuneration credited to partner (tag 6d3236ec), in a voucher also carrying a line on their remuneration_ledger. The s.40(b)(v) book-profit limit is NOT computed here.

Interest + remuneration credited to partner (tag 6d3236ec) in the year, gross: each voucher's net credit to the partner, a reversal lowering nothing -- the s.194T base (salary, remuneration, commission, bonus and interest to a partner). It may be wrong in either direction: see this partner's s.194T question.
Sum of interest_credited_<partner> across all partners -- cross-check this against a shared interest_ledger's own TB movement when every partner uses the same ledger name.

Whether a line on a ledger the client's statutory dues classify as TDS payable appears on a voucher touching partner (tag 6d3236ec)'s capital, interest or remuneration ledgers ("not judged" when none is classified, or when the only such lines are on a ledger shared by partners, on a voucher whose TDS is not booked against partners' capitals alone).

figures.value: not computed: s.40(b) is not computed for 1 partner(s)
figures.definition_text: The sum of the s.40(b) excess across the firm's partners is not stated: it would leave out the partners whose excess is not computed (their s40b_not_computed findings), or no partner is configured (see that question). Where a partner's excess is computed, it is that partner's own figure.

findings.title_text: Remuneration to working partners: the s.40(b)(v) limit depends on book profit, not computed here
limits_text: The s.40(b)(v) remuneration ceiling is a slab on 'book profit' (s.28-44D profit plus remuneration debited, per Explanation 3), which this test does not compute; whether remuneration is authorised and quantified by the deed, and from what date, is a deed reading, not a books fact.

The s.40(b)(v) ceiling (s.40(b)(v) as amended by the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, from AY 2025-26): on the first ₹6 lakh of book profit (or a loss), ₹3 lakh or 90% of the book profit, whichever is more; on the balance, 60%. It applies to the firm's book profit, which this test does not compute, so no limit is stated here.

Partner (tag 6d3236ec): 1 remuneration voucher(s) also credit a ledger this test does not read (Journal M2 on 2025-10-15): remuneration_credited_6d3236ec may be net of it. If that ledger is TDS on this partner's remuneration alone, classify it as TDS payable in the client's statutory dues.
ask_client_text: Provide the computation of book profit under s.40(b) Explanation 3, and the deed clause authorising and quantifying remuneration.

findings.title_text: Payments/credits to a partner whose s.194T base is not read exactly with no TDS ledger line seen
limits_text: Books only: TAN registration, challans filed and any Form 26A route are not visible from vouchers.

2 interest or remuneration voucher(s) also credit a ledger this test does not read (Journal M1 on 2025-09-15, Journal M2 on 2025-10-15): the partner may be credited net of it, so this base may be understated.
2 voucher(s) touching this partner are not read exactly (Journal M1 on 2025-09-15, Journal M2 on 2025-10-15): this base may be wrong in either direction.
This base (₹9,000) is under the s.194T threshold (₹20,000) as read, but it may be wrong (above), so whether it crosses the threshold is not computed.
ask_client_text: The partner's interest and remuneration for the year, and the TDS deducted on each.
Confirm the firm's TAN and whether TDS under s.194T was deposited (this is not visible from the books shown here if it went through a ledger not captured in touched_vouchers).
If not deducted, confirm whether Form 26A relief is available (partner returned the income, tax paid).

findings.title_text: s.40(b) not computed for partner (tag 6d3236ec): its interest credited cannot be read exactly; the CA computes it
limits_text: This test computes the s.40(b) excess for no partner: its reading of a partner's interest from the books can miss or misread some bookings (another partner's interest or remuneration ledger crediting this partner's capital, or a ledger configured in two roles), so no excess it computed would be safe to list in clause 21(c). The CA computes the excess from the deed, the capital accounts and the interest credited. What this test could see is named below, and the interest credited and allowable-interest figures are working figures only.

1 voucher(s) on this partner's capital are not of the plain shape this test reads exactly (Journal M2 on 2025-10-15): this partner's own interest or remuneration ledger debited, its own capital credited, and TDS on a ledger classified as TDS payable, balanced. Each carries a line this test does not read as plain, so the interest counted may be wrong in either direction.

This test reads only that plain shape. Correct bookings of other shapes are not computed here either: a year-end journal crediting several partners at once, a reversal or correction, interest on per-partner ledgers in one journal, one TDS line for several partners, TDS booked through the capital, or a round-off. The CA computes the excess from the vouchers named.

1 interest voucher(s) also credit a ledger this test does not read (Journal M1 on 2025-09-15; ledger tag(s) 87f1d1b4): the partner may be credited net of it, so the interest counted may be understated. If the ledger is TDS on this partner's interest alone, classify it as TDS payable in the client's statutory dues and the interest is counted gross; on a voucher that credits several partners the TDS is not divided, and if it is a payable, a round-off or a payment, the CA reads the interest from the voucher.
No s.40(b) excess is stated for this partner, and none is listed in clause 21(c). Its interest credited and allowable-interest figures are marked not usable for s.40(b).
ask_client_text: The s.40(b) computation for this partner: the deed's authorised interest rate, the capital balances through the year, and the interest credited.
The partner's interest for the year, with the interest and remuneration in each voucher named here and the TDS on each.
If 'Sundry Payable' carries TDS on this partner's interest, classify it as TDS payable in your statutory dues; otherwise, what it is.
